# RabbitMQ

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_component_agents.py from xrds/rabbitmq.meta.yaml; edit the sidecar, not this file. -->

attach mode: a user + permissions on an existing shared broker, scoped to this app's own queue prefix and exchanges. broker mode (no outputs below apply): the shared broker itself.

## How it is requested

A `components[]` entry in an app's values file; the airframe-application chart renders the XR in the app's namespace. Wire it into the app with `env[].fromComponent` (never hand-write the derived names).

## Outputs

- `username`: Secret `{name}-user-credentials`, key `username`.
- `password`: Secret `{name}-user-credentials`, key `password`.
- `host`: ConfigMap `{name}-connection`, key `host`.
- `port`: ConfigMap `{name}-connection`, key `port`.
- `vhost`: ConfigMap `{name}-connection`, key `vhost`.

## Where named objects come from

- Secret `{name}-user-credentials`: created by an operator from the composed User (when `spec.mode` is `attach`).
- ConfigMap `{name}-connection`: composed by this composition (when `spec.mode` is `attach`).
- Service `{name}`: created by an operator from the composed RabbitmqCluster (when `spec.mode` is `broker`).

## Conditions

Besides Crossplane's Ready and Synced. Reasons are a closed set:

- `ComponentReady`: `RabbitMQAttachReady` (True), `RabbitMQAttachProvisioning` (False), `RabbitMQBrokerReady` (True), `RabbitMQBrokerProvisioning` (False).

## Verify a live XR

```
tools/airframe-verify rabbitmq <namespace>/<name> [--context CTX]
```

Read-only. Steps, after the implicit `xr-synced` check:

- `xr-ready` (condition): The RabbitMQ XR's ComponentReady condition has reason RabbitMQAttachReady (attach) or RabbitMQBrokerReady (broker).
- `secret-exists` (secretKeys): Secret {name}-user-credentials exists in the app namespace and has non-empty username and password keys. Only when `spec.mode` is `attach`.
- `configmap-exists` (configMapKeys): ConfigMap {name}-connection exists in the app namespace with host/port/vhost keys. Only when `spec.mode` is `attach`.
- `broker-reachable` (tcp): The broker's {name} Service accepts an AMQP TCP connection on 5672, through kubectl port-forward, so it proves the server is listening, not that the app namespace's NetworkPolicy admits the app. Only when `spec.mode` is `broker`.

## Known failures

- `RabbitMQTopologyWebhookUnavailable` (Synced=False): The RabbitMQ messaging-topology operator's admission webhook did not answer, so Crossplane could not apply a User, Vhost or Permission. The broker and existing credentials are unaffected; ComponentReady keeps its last value. Check the operator: kubectl -n rabbitmq-system get pods,endpointslices -l app.kubernetes.io/name=messaging-topology-operator. It runs two replicas; if both are down, look for leader-election losses in their logs. The XR re-syncs on its own.

## Editing this composition

- Edit `compositions/rabbitmq/templates/`, never the inline blocks in `composition.yaml`: `python3 tools/build-compositions rabbitmq` splices them.
- `python3 tools/test_compositions.py --update rabbitmq` regenerates `example/expected/`; review that diff like code, it is the behaviour change.
- `python3 tools/test_sidecars.py` fails if a template change breaks a name this sidecar promises.
- Shared with other compositions (symlinks into `compositions/_shared/`): `00-readiness-context.yaml`.
- Never end a Go-template comment with a right-trim marker right before apiVersion: v0.3.128 shipped a RabbitmqCluster with no apiVersion that way.
- Attach mode composes a Usage that blocks deleting the broker while attachers exist. The topology operator's webhook fails closed: an outage shows as Synced=False with RabbitMQTopologyWebhookUnavailable.
